title: What you can say. What you cannot

steps.text: Maria asks, "Is this house worth the price?" You do not know. Good news: you do not have to answer.
You ask friendly questions. You do A.L.M. You set appointments. That is your whole job on the phone.

cards.back: Friendly questions to learn what the lead wants.
Appointment, Location, Motivation. You learn it soon.
A set day and time with the agent.

steps.text: A license is a permit from the state. Your agent has one. You do not. So some topics are only for the agent.

cards.back: Never say what a home is worth.
Never give legal or loan advice.
A home checkup. Never explain the report.
Never negotiate. Never talk about commission, the agent's pay.

steps.text: Hard question? Send it to your agent.
steps.sub: The agent has the license. You set the meeting.

steps.line: Great question for your agent. Let's set a time to talk with them.

steps.says: Is this house worth the price?

options.text: Yes, it is a great price.
options.why: That is a price opinion. Only the agent gives one.

options.text: Great question for your agent. Would Saturday at 11 or 2 work?
options.why: You sent it to the agent. You asked for a time.

options.text: I think it is a bit high.
options.why: Never say what a home is worth.

steps.says: The inspection found a roof problem. Is that bad?

options.text: Great question for your agent. I will tell them today.
options.why: You did not guess. The agent will help.

options.text: Roofs are easy to fix. Don't worry.
options.why: You explained an inspection. That is not your job.

steps.q: A lead asks, "Will the seller take less?" What do you do?
options: Send the question to your agent
steps.why: That is negotiating. Only the agent negotiates.

steps.q: A lead asks, "Are you the agent?" What do you say?
options: No, I am on the agent's team.
steps.why: Always tell the truth. Never say you are the agent.

steps.h: A hard question comes. Put your steps in order
items: Ask for a day and time
Write the question in your note

steps.text: Fair housing is a US law. Every person gets the same help. So you treat every lead the same.
Never describe an area by its people, schools, crime or safety. Even a nice word can break the rule.

options.text: Yes, very safe. Good families live there.
options.why: You described the area by safety and people.

options.text: No, I would not live there.
options.why: That is your opinion about an area. Never give one.

options.text: Great question for your agent. I can also send you public sources.
options.why: You stayed fair. You still helped.

items.text: How many bedrooms do you need?
The schools there are the best.
Lots of young families live there.
It is a quiet, safe street.

steps.q: What do you write in your notes?
options: What the lead wants in the home
steps.why: Write what they want in the home. Not who they are.

steps.text: Talk about the home. Never about the people.
steps.sub: This keeps every lead treated the same.

steps.line: Great question for your agent. I can also send you public sources.

steps.text: Lead names, phones and emails belong to your client. They stay inside the client's tools. Never copy, download or share them.

items.text: Send a lead list to my email
Take a photo of my screen
Share a login in a chat

steps.q: You think you shared client data by mistake. What do you do?
options: Fix it and tell no one
steps.why: Fast and honest is always best. Your coordinator will help.

steps.text: Nice work! You know what to say and what to send to your agent.

quiz.q: A lead asks what a home is worth. What do you say?
quiz.explain: Never give a price opinion. Send it to your agent.
You ask questions, do A.L.M. and set appointments.

quiz.q: A lead asks, "Is the area safe?" What do you do?
options: Send it to your agent and offer public sources
quiz.explain: Never describe an area by safety or people.

options: What the lead wants in the home
quiz.explain: Write about the home they want. Not who they are.
Never copy, download or share client data.
